title: King + Rook vs King
description: Master the box method and rook barrier technique to force the enemy king to the edge.

steps.title: The Cut-Off Barrier
steps.instruction: To box in the enemy king, your first goal is establishing an impassable wall along a rank or file with your rook.
steps.explanation: Notice how the rook on the 4th rank creates a horizontal fence preventing Black's king from advancing.

steps.title: Establish the Fence
steps.instruction: Your turn! Move the rook from a1 to a4 to establish the fourth-rank barrier.
steps.explanation: Excellent! The fourth rank is completely sealed off.

steps.title: Marching the King
steps.instruction: The rook holds the fence while our king marches forward into opposition to push Black backward.
steps.explanation: King opposition takes away squares directly opposite, compelling the defender to give ground.

steps.title: Claim Direct Opposition
steps.instruction: Move your white king to e4 to confront Black's king directly across the rook barrier.
steps.explanation: Perfect! With White claiming opposition, Black must retreat backward.

steps.title: Shrinking the Box
steps.instruction: Black retreated to e7. Advance your rook to the 5th rank to shrink the box!
steps.explanation: Great job! The enemy king is now confined to ranks 6, 7, and 8.

steps.title: The Final Checkmate
steps.instruction: The black king is trapped on the back rank opposite your king. Deliver checkmate with Ra8#!
steps.explanation: Checkmate! The enemy king has no escape squares.

title: King + Queen vs King
description: Box the king efficiently by placing your queen a knight's move away, avoiding stalemate traps.

steps.title: The Knight's Distance
steps.instruction: A queen placed a knight's move away from the enemy king cuts off the maximum number of squares without giving check.
steps.explanation: From d4, the queen is a knight's jump away from e6, cutting off ranks 4, files d, and the e5 diagonal.

steps.title: Apply the Clamp
steps.instruction: Move your queen to d4 to clamp down on Black's movement.
steps.explanation: Nicely done! Black's king has only 4 legal moves left.

steps.title: Shrinking the Box
steps.instruction: Black's king stepped back to e7. Advance your queen to d5 to confine the king to ranks 7 and 8.
steps.explanation: The box shrinks further, forcing Black into the corner.

steps.title: Beware of Stalemate
steps.instruction: Never place the queen too close when the king is in the corner unless you are delivering checkmate or supported by your king.
steps.explanation: If your queen goes to g6 here, it's stalemate! But Qg7# is checkmate supported by the king on f6.

steps.title: The Kiss of Death
steps.instruction: Deliver checkmate right in the black king's face with Qg7#!
steps.explanation: Checkmate! The queen is safely protected by the king on f6.

title: King Opposition & Key Squares
description: Understand direct opposition, outflanking, and control of critical squares in king and pawn endings.

steps.title: Understanding Opposition
steps.instruction: When two kings face each other with one square between them, the player NOT having to move holds the opposition.
steps.explanation: Holding the opposition forces the defender to yield key invasion squares.

steps.title: Step into Opposition
steps.instruction: Step forward with your king to e4 to claim the opposition.
steps.explanation: Well done! Black is forced to move aside.

steps.title: The Outflanking Technique
steps.instruction: When Black steps sideways to f6, do not follow him directly. Outflank him by advancing to d5!
steps.explanation: Outflanking allows your king to penetrate behind enemy lines.

steps.title: Outflank the Defender
steps.instruction: Play Kd5 to outflank Black and clear a path forward.
steps.explanation: Masterful! You have outflanked the king and secured the winning advance.

title: Pawn Promotion & Square of the Pawn
description: Calculate pawn races instantly using the rule of the square and shouldering techniques.

steps.title: The Rule of the Square
steps.instruction: Count the squares from your passed pawn to the queening square to form a square box. If the enemy king cannot enter this box, the pawn promotes unaided!
steps.explanation: The b6 pawn creates a box from b6 to b8, across to d8, and down to d6. Black's king on e1 is outside the square!

steps.title: Push the Runner
steps.instruction: Advance the passed pawn to b7. Black's king is too slow to catch it!
steps.explanation: Black cannot enter the square in time. The pawn will queen next turn!

steps.title: Shouldering the Enemy King
steps.instruction: When the enemy king tries to chase your pawn, use your king's body to block his diagonal path.
steps.explanation: Playing Ke3 takes away d4 and f4, preventing Black from approaching the e2 pawn.

steps.title: Take the Key Square
steps.instruction: Move your king to e3 to shoulder Black and shield your e-pawn.
steps.explanation: Solid! Black's king is held at bay.

steps.title: Crown the Queen
steps.instruction: Push your b-pawn to b8 and promote to a Queen!
steps.explanation: Promotion achieved! A completely winning advantage.

title: Lucena Position (Building the Bridge)
description: Learn the most famous winning technique in rook endgames: building a rook bridge to shield the king.

steps.title: The Lucena Setup
steps.instruction: In the Lucena position, White has a passed pawn on the 7th rank with the king in front. To win, White must build a bridge with the rook.
steps.explanation: Placing the rook on the 4th rank prepares to intercept vertical checks from Black's rook.

steps.title: The Fourth Rank Bridge
steps.instruction: Play Rf4 to set up the classic bridge-building shelter on the 4th rank.
steps.explanation: Brilliant! The rook is perfectly stationed on the fourth rank.

steps.title: Step the King Out
steps.instruction: Black waits with Rd2. Step your king out of the pawn's path to c7!
steps.explanation: The king steps out, threatening immediate promotion.

steps.title: Interception - The Bridge
steps.instruction: Black checks from behind with Rc2+. Block the check with Rc4 to complete the bridge!
steps.explanation: The bridge is built! Black cannot stop the pawn from queening next move.

title: Philidor Defense (Third Rank Defense)
description: Learn the essential drawing technique against rook and pawn by anchoring your rook on the third rank.

steps.title: The Defensive Barrier
steps.instruction: As Black defending against an advanced pawn, keep your rook on the 6th rank (your 3rd rank) to block the White king from invading.
steps.explanation: White cannot advance their king past the 5th rank without pushing the pawn first.

steps.title: Maintain the Horizontal Clamp
steps.instruction: Slide your rook along the 6th rank to b6 to wait safely.
steps.explanation: Well held! The white king has no shelter on the 6th rank.

steps.title: When the Pawn Pushes, Drop Back
steps.instruction: White pushed e6! Now the pawn blocks their own king from checks from behind. Drop your rook to the 1st rank immediately!
steps.explanation: From the 1st rank, Black will give perpetual vertical checks from behind.

steps.title: Drop Your Rook to the Rear
steps.instruction: Move your rook from b6 down to b1.
steps.explanation: Excellent! You are now positioned to deliver endless rear checks.

steps.title: The Perpetual Check
steps.instruction: White tries Kd5. Check the exposed king with Rd1+ to seal the draw!
steps.explanation: Draw secured! The white king cannot escape the hail of vertical checks.

title: Bishop + Knight Checkmate
description: Coordinate minor pieces to drive the enemy king into a corner matching your bishop's square color.

steps.title: The Corner of the Bishop's Color
steps.instruction: You can only force checkmate in a corner that matches your bishop's color (here, light squares: a1 or h8).
steps.explanation: Black's king on a1 is already trapped in the correct light-squared corner.

steps.title: Seal the Diagonal
steps.instruction: Play Bd4+ to take away the king's flight squares along the long diagonal.
steps.explanation: Check! The enemy king is confined strictly to the corner.

steps.title: The W-Maneuver
steps.instruction: The knight hops in a W-shaped pattern across the board to take away the dark squares that the bishop cannot control.
steps.explanation: From e7 and c7, the knight covers the dark squares, guiding the king to checkmate.

steps.title: Close the Net
steps.instruction: Hop your knight to e7 to take away c8 and d7.
steps.explanation: Superb! The king is completely immobilized.

title: Rook + Pawn vs Rook (Tarrasch Rule)
description: Apply Tarrasch's principle: rooks belong behind passed pawns, whether attacking or defending.

steps.title: Tarrasch's Golden Rule
steps.instruction: Siegbert Tarrasch formulated the classic principle: place your rook BEHIND passed pawns — behind your own to push them, behind the opponent's to stop them.
steps.explanation: Behind the pawn, the rook gains mobility as the pawn advances forward.

steps.title: Get Behind Your Passed Pawn
steps.instruction: Move your rook from e1 to a1 to support the a5 pawn from behind.
steps.explanation: Spot on! The rook now shields the pawn's entire journey to promotion.

steps.title: March the Pawn
steps.instruction: Push the passed pawn to a6 under the protection of your rook.
steps.explanation: The pawn advances smoothly with full rook protection.

steps.title: Activate Your King
steps.instruction: Bring your king up to f3 to assist the rook and escort the pawn.
steps.explanation: Active king plus Tarrasch rook ensures a textbook endgame victory.

title: Controlling the Center
description: Understand why e4, d4, e5, and d5 dictate opening play and learn to establish central pawn duos.

steps.title: The Four Central Squares
steps.instruction: The squares e4, d4, e5, and d5 are the center of the chess board. Controlling them grants piece mobility and territory.
steps.explanation: Opening with a central pawn immediately claims space and frees your queen and bishop.

steps.title: Stake Your Central Claim
steps.instruction: Advance your king's pawn two squares to e4.
steps.explanation: Strong start! e4 controls d5 and f5 while opening pathways.

steps.title: Establish the Classical Pawn Duo
steps.instruction: Black played 1...Nf6. Expand your central dominance with d4!
steps.explanation: The dream central duo (e4 + d4) controls c5, d5, e5, and f5.

steps.title: Develop with Central Support
steps.instruction: Develop your knight to c3 to reinforce e4 and control the center.
steps.explanation: Pieces developed toward the center exert maximum influence.

title: Minor Piece Development & Castling
description: Follow the golden rules: knights before bishops, king safety first, and rapid harmonious development.

steps.title: Knights Before Bishops
steps.instruction: Knights develop to natural central squares (f3/c3), while bishops need the right diagonal chosen depending on the opponent's setup.
steps.explanation: Nf3 attacks e5 and prepares kingside castling.

steps.title: Develop the King's Knight
steps.instruction: Play Nf3 to attack e5 and develop your minor piece.
steps.explanation: Active and purposeful development!

steps.title: Develop the Bishop to an Active Diagonal
steps.instruction: Develop your light-squared bishop to c4, aiming at Black's weak f7 square.
steps.explanation: The Italian Bishop puts direct pressure on Black's vulnerable pawn.

steps.title: Castle for King Safety
steps.instruction: Now that minor pieces are out, tuck your king away safely by castling kingside (O-O).
steps.explanation: King is safe behind three pawns, and your rook is ready for action!

title: Avoiding Early Queen Outings & Traps
description: Punish premature queen attacks and defend against cheap tactical tricks like Scholar's Mate.

steps.title: The Danger of Early Queen Attacks
steps.instruction: White brought their queen to f3 on move 2 hunting for Scholar's Mate. Early queen sorties waste time and invite counter-attacks.
steps.explanation: White threatens Qxf7#. Defend calmly while developing a minor piece.

steps.title: Block the Threat and Develop
steps.instruction: Play Nf6 to block the queen's battery on f7 while developing your knight.
steps.explanation: Perfect! Threat eliminated and your kingside knight is active.

steps.title: Punish the Overextended Queen
steps.instruction: White wastes another move with h3. Jump your knight to d4, attacking both the queen on f3 and the c2 fork square!
steps.explanation: Crushing! The queen must flee while c2 is under severe threat.

steps.title: Strike in the Center
steps.instruction: White retreated the queen back to d1. Strike boldly in the center with d5!
steps.explanation: Outstanding! Black has superior development, central space, and a decisive lead.

title: Piece Activity & Outposts
description: Establish dominant outposts for knights and coordinate pieces to maximize board control.

steps.title: What is an Outpost?
steps.instruction: An outpost is a square on the 4th, 5th, or 6th rank defended by a pawn that cannot be attacked by an enemy pawn.
steps.explanation: e5 is a permanent outpost because Black's pawns on d5 and f7 cannot kick the knight away.

steps.title: Plant Your Knight on the Outpost
steps.instruction: Move your knight to the e5 outpost to dominate the center.
steps.explanation: Monstrous knight! It controls key squares deep in Black's camp.

steps.title: Remove Black's Counter-Piece
steps.instruction: Black challenges with Nd7. Capture on d7 to retain spatial superiority.
steps.explanation: Crisp exchange. Black's minor pieces remain cramped.

steps.title: Lock Down the Queenside Space
steps.instruction: Push c5 to clamp down Black's queenside expansion.
steps.explanation: Total spatial dominance achieved!

title: Open Files & 7th Rank Rooks
description: Seize open files with your heavy pieces and infiltrate the deadly 7th rank.

steps.title: Seizing the Open File
steps.instruction: An open file has no pawns on it. Rooks must occupy open files to prepare invasion routes.
steps.explanation: The c-file is the only fully open file on the board.

steps.title: Occupy the C-File
steps.instruction: Move your rook from f1 to c1 to control the c-file.
steps.explanation: Mastery of the open file begins with solid placement.

steps.title: Double the Heavy Artillery
steps.instruction: Place your queen on c2 behind the rook to dominate the file.
steps.explanation: Doubling on the open file creates overwhelming pressure.

steps.title: Infiltrate the 7th Rank
steps.instruction: Invade the 7th rank with Qc7, attacking Black's pawn base!
steps.explanation: Infiltration complete! The 7th rank yields decisive tactical shots.

title: Pawn Structure & Weaknesses
description: Identify structural flaws like isolated and backward pawns, and execute blockades to win material.

steps.title: The Isolated Pawn Weakness
steps.instruction: An isolated pawn has no friendly pawns on neighboring files. It cannot be defended by another pawn and requires piece babysitting.
steps.explanation: Exchanging on d5 isolates Black's d-pawn permanently.

steps.title: Isolate the Enemy Pawn
steps.instruction: Play cxd5 to saddle Black with an isolated queen's pawn.
steps.explanation: Black recaptures with exd5, leaving d5 permanently isolated!

steps.title: Blockade the Weakness
steps.instruction: Nimzowitsch rule: always blockade an isolated pawn! Place your knight on the d4 square right in front of the pawn.
steps.explanation: A firmly anchored knight blockades the pawn and controls the center.

steps.title: Solidify the Center
steps.instruction: Reinforce your central structure with f4 to secure the knight forever.
steps.explanation: The stronghold is impenetrable. Black's pawn weakness is permanently exploited.
